groups.title: あ row

chars.mnemonic: An antenna with a cross on top and a loop below: "a" for antenna.
Two eels swimming side by side: "ee" as in eel.
A person bent over going "ooh", with a little hat on top.
An exotic bird with a long swooping tail: "e" for exotic.
A golfer about to tee off: the ball is the little tick on the right. "Oh!"

groups.note: Every hiragana is one beat (mora). Vowels are short and pure: a as in "father", i as in "machine", u as in "flute" (lips relaxed), e as in "bed", o as in "more".

chars.mnemonic: A karate kick: the hooked leg and a short chopping stroke.
A key: two bars across a shaft, with a small loop at the bottom.
A bird's beak opening to say "coo".
A keg of beer standing next to a stick.
Two koi fish swimming one above the other.

groups.title: さ row

chars.mnemonic: A samurai sword with its crossguard.
A fishing hook: "she" caught a fish.
A swing hanging from a bar: Sue on a swing.
A set of bars like a gate: "se" for set.
A zigzag sewing stitch: "so" and sew.

groups.note: し is "shi", not "si". Romaji in this app follows Hepburn, which spells sounds the way English speakers expect.

groups.title: た row

chars.mnemonic: It looks like "ta" written in Latin letters: a t and an a.
A cheerleader with a round skirt: "chi".
A tsunami wave curling over.
A telephone cord hanging from a hook.
A toe with a splinter stuck in it.

groups.note: ち is "chi" and つ is "tsu". The つ sound is like the "ts" at the end of "cats".

chars.mnemonic: A nun kneeling, with a cross beside her: "na".
A needle beside two short threads: "nee".
Noodles twirled around chopsticks, with a loop at the end.
A cat (neko) sitting with its tail curled underneath.
A "no entry" sign: a circle with a stroke through it.

groups.title: は row

chars.mnemonic: A stick next to a letter "t" with a loop: someone laughing "ha!"
A big smile: "hee hee".
Mount Fuji with wisps of cloud around it.
A heap: a small hill with a peak.
A house with a stick fence: "ho-me".

groups.note: ふ is "fu": blow the sound out gently between the lips, not with the teeth. Note: は is read "wa" when it is the topic particle (わたしは).

chars.mnemonic: A mast with two crossbars and a loop: "ma".
A rope tied in a loop around me: "mee".
A cow going "moo", with a curled tail.
An eye (me) with a long lash across it.
A hook with more bars across it: "mo" for more.
A yak's head with a horn sticking up: "ya".
A fish making a U-turn: "you".
A yo-yo hanging from its string.

groups.title: ら row

chars.mnemonic: A rabbit's ear and curled body: "ra".
Two reeds standing in water: "ree".
A loop at the end of the road: "ru".
A runner's leg kicking back: "re".
A road with a sharp bend: "ro". Like る without the loop.

groups.note: The Japanese r is a light tap of the tongue, between English r, l and d. It is never rolled.

groups.title: わ・を・ん

chars.mnemonic: A person waving with a rounded arm: "wa". Like れ with a closed curve.
A toe stepping into water: "wo-ah!" Used only as the object particle, pronounced "o".
An "n" that slid off its chair. The only kana with no vowel.

words.meaning: to read a book (を marks the object)

groups.note: を is used only as the object particle and is pronounced "o". ん is its own beat: ほん is two beats, ho-n. へ is read "e" when it marks a direction.

groups.title: が row (dakuten)
groups.intro: Two small dots (dakuten ゛) at the top right turn k into g.

chars.mnemonic: か with two dots (dakuten) becomes ga. Same shape, voiced sound.
き with two dots (dakuten) becomes gi. Same shape, voiced sound.
く with two dots (dakuten) becomes gu. Same shape, voiced sound.
け with two dots (dakuten) becomes ge. Same shape, voiced sound.
こ with two dots (dakuten) becomes go. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.note: Dakuten (゛) voice the consonant: k → g, s → z, t → d, h → b. Voiced sounds use the voice box; put a finger on your throat and feel it buzz.

groups.title: ざ row (dakuten)
groups.intro: The dakuten turns s into z. Note じ is "ji", not "zi".

chars.mnemonic: さ with two dots (dakuten) becomes za. Same shape, voiced sound.
し with two dots (dakuten) becomes ji. Same shape, voiced sound.
す with two dots (dakuten) becomes zu. Same shape, voiced sound.
せ with two dots (dakuten) becomes ze. Same shape, voiced sound.
そ with two dots (dakuten) becomes zo. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.title: だ row (dakuten)
groups.intro: The dakuten turns t into d. ぢ and づ are rare and sound like じ and ず.

chars.mnemonic: た with two dots (dakuten) becomes da. Same shape, voiced sound.
ち with two dots (dakuten) becomes ji. Same shape, voiced sound.
つ with two dots (dakuten) becomes zu. Same shape, voiced sound.
て with two dots (dakuten) becomes de. Same shape, voiced sound.
と with two dots (dakuten) becomes do. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.title: ば row (dakuten)
groups.intro: The dakuten turns h into b.

chars.mnemonic: は with two dots (dakuten) becomes ba. Same shape, voiced sound.
ひ with two dots (dakuten) becomes bi. Same shape, voiced sound.
ふ with two dots (dakuten) becomes bu. Same shape, voiced sound.
へ with two dots (dakuten) becomes be. Same shape, voiced sound.
ほ with two dots (dakuten) becomes bo. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.title: ぱ row (handakuten)
groups.intro: A small circle (handakuten ゜) turns h into p.

chars.mnemonic: は with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pa. Same shape, voiced sound.
ひ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pi. Same shape, voiced sound.
ふ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pu. Same shape, voiced sound.
へ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pe. Same shape, voiced sound.
ほ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes po. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.note: The handakuten (゜) is a small circle. It appears only on the は row and makes p sounds.

groups.title: Combinations (きゃ, しゅ, ちょ…)
groups.intro: Combine an i-row kana with a small ゃ, ゅ or ょ. The two symbols make one beat.

chars.mnemonic: き (ki) + small ゃ = kya, said as one beat.
き (ki) + small ゅ = kyu, said as one beat.
き (ki) + small ょ = kyo, said as one beat.
し (shi) + small ゃ = sha, said as one beat.
し (shi) + small ゅ = shu, said as one beat.
し (shi) + small ょ = sho, said as one beat.
ち (chi) + small ゃ = cha, said as one beat.
ち (chi) + small ゅ = chu, said as one beat.
ち (chi) + small ょ = cho, said as one beat.
に (ni) + small ゃ = nya, said as one beat.
に (ni) + small ゅ = nyu, said as one beat.
に (ni) + small ょ = nyo, said as one beat.
ひ (hi) + small ゃ = hya, said as one beat.
ひ (hi) + small ゅ = hyu, said as one beat.
ひ (hi) + small ょ = hyo, said as one beat.
み (mi) + small ゃ = mya, said as one beat.
み (mi) + small ゅ = myu, said as one beat.
み (mi) + small ょ = myo, said as one beat.
り (ri) + small ゃ = rya, said as one beat.
り (ri) + small ゅ = ryu, said as one beat.
り (ri) + small ょ = ryo, said as one beat.

groups.note: A full-size kana followed by a small ゃ, ゅ or ょ blends into a single beat: きゃ is one beat, きや is two. Compare びょういん (hospital) with びよういん (hair salon).

groups.title: Voiced combinations (ぎゃ, じゅ, びょ…)
groups.intro: The same pattern with dakuten and handakuten kana. じゃ, じゅ, じょ are "ja, ju, jo".

chars.mnemonic: ぎ (gi) + small ゃ = gya, said as one beat.
ぎ (gi) + small ゅ = gyu, said as one beat.
ぎ (gi) + small ょ = gyo, said as one beat.
じ (ji) + small ゃ = ja, said as one beat.
じ (ji) + small ゅ = ju, said as one beat.
じ (ji) + small ょ = jo, said as one beat.
び (bi) + small ゃ = bya, said as one beat.
び (bi) + small ゅ = byu, said as one beat.
び (bi) + small ょ = byo, said as one beat.
ぴ (pi) + small ゃ = pya, said as one beat.
ぴ (pi) + small ゅ = pyu, said as one beat.
ぴ (pi) + small ょ = pyo, said as one beat.

groups.title: Small っ (double consonants)
groups.intro: Small っ marks a doubled consonant: the sound stops for one beat.

chars.mnemonic: A small つ. It is not pronounced; it doubles the next consonant by holding a one-beat pause.

groups.note: Small っ is a silent beat: hold the pause before the next consonant. がっこう is four beats: ga-(pause)-ko-o. Writing it full size (つ) changes the word.

groups.title: Long vowels
groups.intro: Vowel length changes meaning. Train your ear to hear one beat versus two.

chars.mnemonic: Add あ to hold an a-sound for two beats: おかあさん.
Add い to hold an i-sound: おにいさん, おおきい.
Add う to hold a u-sound: くうき, ゆうめい.
A long e is usually written with い: せんせい, えいが. Hold the e; the i is barely heard.
A long o is usually written with う: おとうさん, とうきょう. A few words use お: おおきい, とおい.

groups.note: Long vowels are held for two beats. They are written by adding あ, い, う, え or お: おばさん (aunt) and おばあさん (grandmother) differ only in length. "ou" is pronounced as a long o, and "ei" as a long e.
